title: Observability Security And Operations Master Roadmap
goal: Coordinate Debian observability, unified runtime logging, MCP debugging and defensive incident response into one backend-first operations program for Odysseus.

source_roadmaps.title: Debian Observability And Active Security Roadmap
source_roadmaps.role: Infrastructure layer: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, log agent, Podman metrics and CrowdSec.

source_roadmaps.title: Unified Runtime Logging And MCP Debugging Roadmap
source_roadmaps.role: Data and tool layer: unified redacted events, Telegram diagnostics, read-only MCP debugging and debug bundles.

source_roadmaps.title: Security Incident Response And Escalation Roadmap
source_roadmaps.role: Decision layer: escalation ladder, incident model, response policy and gated remediation.

design_principles: Backend and logic first; no new UI in this program.
Podman pods, not Docker, are the operational assumption.
Promtail must not be introduced as a new component; prefer Grafana Alloy, Fluent Bit or OpenTelemetry Collector.
All event/log/diagnostic output must be redacted by default.
MCP debugging is full-featured but read-only by default.
Any remediation, restart, firewall, CrowdSec, deploy, rollback, token rotation or live write action requires a gate.
DSGVO/incident mode forces local-only handling for sensitive evidence.

execution_order.reason: Before anything ships to Loki or becomes MCP-visible, map current logs and privacy risk.
Map attacker scenarios to evidence and response limits while the log inventory is fresh.
Shared event envelope is the contract for all later telemetry, MCP and incident response.
Define safe low-cardinality Loki/Prometheus labels before broad ingestion.
Incident and action objects can be built against the event envelope.
Response permissions and blocked actions must exist before any remediation tooling.
Telegram is the most important first end-to-end diagnostic flow.
Scheduler, inbox, Nextcloud and memory are the recurring operational pain points.
RaptorGraph and long-term memory need provenance-aware diagnostics.
Classifiers need enough unified events to classify real system behavior.
Read-only MCP debugging becomes useful once event sources exist.
Debug bundles package correlated evidence for incidents and operator review.
Notifications should use incident model, policy and debug bundle references.
Incident MCP tools extend the debug MCP surface after base MCP diagnostics are stable.
Runbooks document operator gates before remediation plans are prepared.
Prepare-only remediation can be implemented after policies, MCP and runbooks are clear.
Read-only server inventory can be performed when operator grants a bounded live gate.
Install/configure observability and CrowdSec only after repo contracts and live gates are ready.
Live observability read adapters depend on configured Prometheus/Loki endpoints.
Run live validation only after repo tests and explicit operator Go.

phase_0_safe_parallel.condition: Docs/inventory only; no live server access without gate.
Coordinate model field names; avoid changing MCP or Telegram files.

phase_1_safe_parallel.condition: All use the event envelope; avoid same files in memory services.

phase_2_serial_hot_paths.reason: MCP server and tool policy must remain coherent.

phase_3_live_gated.condition: Requires explicit operator live Go per gate.

blocks: Any automatic or operator-approved CrowdSec ban/unban execution

master_definition_of_done: Odysseus has a unified redacted event envelope across major runtime subsystems.
Telegram, scheduler, inbox, memory, RaptorGraph and model failures are traceable by correlation_id.
A read-only MCP debug workbench can diagnose incidents and operational failures.
Security incidents have a structured escalation ladder, response policy and operator-gated actions.
Debian observability provides host, Podman, log, CrowdSec and Odysseus runtime evidence.
No live remediation or public exposure is enabled without explicit gates.

recommended_next_action.reason: ULOG-0, ULOG-1, ULOG-7, SIR-0 and SIR-1 are complete; the next repo-only slice is the incident response policy engine before classifiers, notifications or MCP incident tools.
